answer: Every facility carries `managed-by` (system|user, default system); only user-created facilities can be user-deleted. Created for you: line-ptp, trib-ptp and flexo default to managed-by system, and the odu page states "The high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created". You add by hand: the super-channel (`add super-channel-<name> carriers <v> carrier-mode <v>`), then low-order ODUs (`add odu-<name> odu-type ODU4i|ODUflexi|ODU4|ODUflex parent-odu <HO-ODU> time-slots <1..255>`), the line OTU (`add otu-1-5-L1-1-OTU4-1 parent flexo-group-1-5-L1-1 time-slots 1`) and the xcon. The stated pre-condition is: "Super-channel must be added before Low Order ODUs can be added." Check what exists with `show facilities` and `show odu`.

BERT: `bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=egress test-duration=10` (Operational Mode). test-signal-type none|PRBS31|PRBS31NONINV|scrambled-idles (default none); monitoring-type adds fec-frames; test-duration min 10 s, max 1000 hrs, 0 = indefinite. Then `bert stop test-id=TestX` (test-id mandatory), `bert get`, `bert delete`. Test pattern injection also lives on `set odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction> test-signal-type` (none|PRBS31Q|PRBS13Q|scrambled-idles|PRBS9|PRBS31|PRBS31NONINV, default none), test-signal-direction ingress|egress|both (default ingress), test-signal-monitoring true|false (default false). Loopback: `set otu-<name> loopback none|facility|terminal` (default none) with loopback-mode loopback|loopback-and-continue; optical-carrier also has loopback none|facility|terminal.

The facility must exist and be named as the supporting-facility, and the far end must be identified: `add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <facility> remote-secure-entity <AID> enabled true`. remote-secure-entity is the AID of the remote optical carrier (1830 GX G40), the remote ODU (G30), or the remote OTUflex for CHM7/CHM7X L1 service encryption. enabled defaults to false, alarm-report-control defaults to inhibited, re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s (default 28800), re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic|continue-traffic (default continue-traffic), traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s (default 0). Certificates must be in place at each end: a local-certificate as the node's identity plus a peer-certificate, which "represents a trusted 'remote peer' certificate for L1 encryption secure application", loaded with `import-certificate`. Verify with `show data-path-encryption` and `show secure-entity-<name> oper-state`.

The telemetry object covers persistent and dynamic telemetry: `show telemetry` and `set telemetry id <string>` (0..4096 chars). It is system-managed and cannot be manually deleted. `show subscriptions` lists the subscription set. Per subscription: `show current-subscription-<subscription-name> [related-session-id] [related-dial-out-server] [session-type] [session-protocol] [encoding] [transfer-mode] [updates-only] [user-access]`, where session-type is gnmi-dial-in, gnmi-dial-out-tunnel or gnmi-dial-out-reverse-rpc, session-protocol gnmi, encoding json|bytes|proto|ascii|json-ietf (default json-ietf), transfer-mode stream|once|poll (default stream), updates-only default false. What each one watches: `show subscription-path-<subscription-name>/<subscription-path-name>` giving subscription-path, subscription-path-origin, subscription-path-mode target-defined|on-change|sample (default target-defined), sample-interval and heartbeat-interval in ms (default 0), suppress-redundant (default true).

At rest the database is encrypted: `show db-protection-scheme` reports encryption-algorithm xts-aes-256-plain64 (AES-256 in XTS mode), integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512 or none, integrity-status passed-on-bootup|failed-on-bootup|disabled, and mode encryption-only or encryption-with-integrity, changeable via the db-migrate RPC. Before you can take a copy, the db-passphrase must be set: "The system will only accept this command if the db-passphrase (used for DB snapshot encryption) is configured, either in global configuration (as part of the security-policies), or locally as a parameter of this command." So use `set security-policies db-passphrase` (40..200 chars, minimum 40, no dictionary words, Z85 character set) or `take-snapshot db-passphrase=***`. Automatic snapshots stay disabled until it is set. `take-snapshot [db-instance=]<temp|manual|onehour|oneday|oneweek|rollback>` (default temp) with optional description; list results with `show database`.

Start at the RIB: `show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family]`. Each RIB holds one address family (ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast), and for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family, so the vrf leaf tells you which instance the prefix landed in. Then `show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol]`: source-protocol shows whether it came from OSPF, BGP or static, and special-next-hop none|blackhole|unreachable shows if it is deliberately discarded (for blackhole and unreachable no next-hop is created under the route). Resolve the hop with `show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address]`, for example `show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN`. Cross-check the source with `show ipv4-static-route-<prefix>/<vrf>` (distance 1..255, default 1; monitoring-state unmonitored|ok|failed); the interface's VRF must match the static route's vrf. `show routing` and `show vrf-<name>` (type mgmt|internal) give the wider view.

Password rules come from `show security-policies`: strict-password-check (default true) enforces minimum 8 characters plus at least one lowercase, one uppercase, one number and one symbol, and the username cannot be part of the password; disabled drops all of that to a 1-character minimum. minimum-password-length is 1..200, default 8. enforce-password-history-check (default true) blocks reuse of the previous 5 passwords, with password-history-size 1..200, default 5. These only apply to newly defined passwords. Lockout is per user: `show user-<name>` gives user-status (enabled, disabled, password-aged or lockout, where lockout means the account is locked after unsuccessful logins), failed-logins, max-invalid-login 0..255 default 5, and suspension-time 0..1440 minutes default 5. security-policies also has disable-user-lockout. To clear a stuck session run `show session` and then `kill-session <session-id>` with the id in the form <ip-address>:<port>; you cannot kill your own session, and only SA users see all sessions.

Untouched defaults: log-file keeps number-of-files 10 (range 1..20) and rotates at max-file-size 30 MB (range 1..30), source-facilities all, sensitive-data none (only for log-file-default-audit-dbg), and "By default, severity is set to informational and above". The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted. Console logging is off: `log-console enabled` defaults to false. Remote servers default to enabled true, port 514, transport udp, message-format rfc5424, message-coalescence true, origin manual, sensitive-data none, destination-facility-override disabled. Node-wide syslog defaults: source-address localhost, log-file-message-coalescence true, log-relay false, assignment-method both, niap-compliant-logging false, privacy-mode false. The single switch that kills everything remote is `set syslog remote-logging-switch false`: "If false, disable all remote logging destinations" (default true).

What is raised now: `show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed]`, and `show alarms` / `show alarm-<alarm-id>` for detail (perceived-severity, service-affecting, reported-time, corrective-action, operator-state). Manual clearing: `clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>]`, which only works on the small subset of alarms with no automatic clear criteria; find them with `show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true`. This mechanism applies only to system-wide alarms not associated with a particular resource. `set-alarm-state` changes the operator state of an alarm. Whether inhibiting reporting drops what is already up is decided by `set alarm-control arc-behavior`: clear-alarms means that when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are cleared, leave-alarms leaves them raised. The default is leave-alarms. alarm-control also carries alarm-soaking-behavior automatic|no-soak, default automatic.

The Equipment dashboard is the temperature view: `status equipment` walks chassis, cards and TOMs and prints temperature sensors and power values alongside presence, oper-state and alarms, for example "chassis-1 G42 (NC) temp 25C | power 2.1/4400 W" and "card-1-1 XMM4 (Act) temp 25C". To narrow it, give the chassis id as the filter, for example `status equipment 5`; only existing chassis ids are accepted, wildcards are not supported, so it is either all chassis or exactly one. For the raw sensor readings use `show pm`, whose real-time PM per resource gives temperature (C) with instant/avg/min/max, plus fan-speed (percent) per FAN card and chassis inlet-temperature; filter with a resource such as `show pm card-1-7`. Physically the state shows on the LEDs: `show leds`, `show led status` or `show led-<location>/<name> status`, with values off, green, flashing-green, yellow, flashing-yellow, amber, flashing-amber, red, flashing-red, cycling, cycling-with-off, not-available.

The line is the OTS: `show ots-<name>` gives span-loss-derived-rx and span-loss-derived-tx, the measured span loss based on OSC including losses external to the fiber (0..99 dB, where 99 dB means OLOS, and only relevant when an OSC channel exists). Compare against the configured span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive (0..80 dB, default 0; receive also accepts 99 as not configured, and changing it is traffic affecting). span-loss-reference (configured|measured, default measured) decides which one the system uses to calculate automatic target OXCon powers. span-loss-alarm-threshold (0..80 dB, 99) is set autonomously by the system and persists across reboot; in measured mode force a refresh with `update`. Also useful: span-loss-aging-margin-rx (0..10 dB, default 1.0), external-attenuation-tx/rx (0..30 dB) and fiber-length-derived-rx/tx. The compensation is on the amplifier: `show amplifier-<name>` reports gain-operating and gain-target (0..40 dB), gain-range-actual, gain-adjustment (-20..20 dB), input-power-mon and output-power-mon (-99..99 dBm), tilt-actual, control-state, control-mode auto-max-pw (default) or manual, and span-loss-control (default enabled), which must be enabled when span-loss-reference is measured.

Client side first: trib-ptp is the tributary client physical termination between the transceiver and the protocol layer, carrying the protocol client facility above it (ethernet, otu, fc, stm, eth-zr). That client maps into a mapped or low-order odu, which is joined to the line by an xcon (`add xcon-1 source ethernet-1-4-T1 destination odu-1-4-T1-1-ODUni-1`). On the line side the low-order ODU sits under the high-order ODUCn/ODUCni, which is carried by the line otu (added with `parent flexo-group-...`) and flexo, all supported by line-ptp. The digital domain ends at the optical-carrier / optical-channel under the super-channel and super-channel-group: that is where frequency, tx-power and modulation-format are set. From there the optical domain takes over at the nmc (Network Media Channel), whose parent-facility is a Media Channel or an OMS and which is joined by an oxcon, then oms and ots out to the fiber. Walk it with `show facilities` and each facility's supporting-facilities and supported-facilities.

No, they are two different objects. A counter crossing a limit is PM: `add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter> [low-threshold <value>] [high-threshold <value>]` (also set/show/delete). Values are numbers (uint64, int64, decimal64), na or not-supported, defaulting to na; direction ingress|egress|all|na and location all|na|near-end|far-end both default to all. The TCA itself is armed with `set pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> tca-supervision true|false`, with per-type defaults from `set pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-tca-supervision`. Changing how loudly an existing fault is reported is alarm severity: `set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>`, for example `set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor`, or `set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <value>`. Both alarm-severity objects are system-managed and cannot be manually deleted.

Inhibit reporting on the card with `set card-<name> alarm-report-control inhibited` (values allowed and inhibited); the same alarm-report-control attribute exists on the facilities underneath (otu, odu, trib-ptp, line-ptp, flexo, ots, nmc, amplifier, super-channel), where the default is allowed. What happens to alarms the card has already raised is decided node-wide by `set alarm-control arc-behavior`: with leave-alarms, which is the default, current alarms stay raised when ARC is set to inhibit; with clear-alarms they are cleared. So set `arc-behavior clear-alarms` first if you want the standing alarms to disappear from the NOC as well. You can also put the card itself out of service with `set card-<name> admin-state maintenance` (lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock). Confirm the result with `show current-alarms` and `show card-<name> alarm-report-control admin-state`.

A secure-application "represents an application which uses X509v3 certificate as its digital identity". Run `show secure-application-<id> [type] [active-certificate-id] [in-use] [status] [verify-client-cert]`: active-certificate-id is the list of assigned certificates (string 0..128), and in-use is a leafref to active-certificate-id, that is the one actually presented; type is server or client and status is enabled or disabled. Assign with `set secure-application-WebGUI active-certificate-id client`, or several with `set secure-application-gRPC active-certificate-id certX,certY`. verify-client-cert is disabled or required (default disabled) and must be required for TLS Mutual Authentication; changes apply only to new TLS connections. Before it will come up the certificate has to be imported: `import-certificate local-certificate certificate-name=local-cert-1 <string in PEM format> <passphrase>`, plus its CA chain as trusted-certificate (root certificates must be installed individually; -i pulls in intermediates from a bundle). Verify with `show local-certificate-<id>` status (valid, expired, revoked, untrusted, future, pending-import) and used-by.

Pipe the show output through the csv display filter: `show pm <command flag> | display csv`, which is importable to a spreadsheet such as Excel; `display xml` and `display json` are also available. Restrict it to the 15-minute bins with the pm-15min period filter and the parameter, resource, resource-type, AID or data-type pm-filters (use `show pm <tab>` for the full filter list). Bin 0 is the current data and bins 1 to n are history, with the bin-to-timestamp mapping printed alongside. Useful flags: -t for standard table format, -n=<number-of-records> (default 1000 records per chassis), -s=<skip-records> for paging, -st= and -et= for a timestamp window (format 2021-02-01T10:00:00+01:00), -sbin=/-ebin= for a bin window, and -i=<chassis-name> (only once per command).

Use `show pm-catalog <string>`, where the string is the catalog name. For example `show pm-catalog parameter-undersized` returns:  pm-parameter-undersized, units packets, type counter. The same information is available from the parameter object itself with `show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]`, for example `show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds`, or `show pm-parameter` for the full list. Both are available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Turn data supervision off on that resource: `set pm-control <entity> data-supervision false`, for example `set pm-control pm-resource-card-1-1 data-supervision false`. data-supervision is described as real-time data supervision for the resource, takes true or false and defaults to true. The equivalent per-instance switch is `set pm-resource-<resource> real-time-supervision <true|false>`, also defaulting to true; `show pm-resource-<resource>` displays resource-type, AID, real-time-supervision and real-time-data-last-reset. Both commands work in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode, and `show pm-control` lists every resource in the system that supports PM data.

Yes. pm-control-entry configures PM for one particular resource, for one particular period, direction and location, so use `set pm-control-entry-<resource>/pm-15min/ingress/near-end tca-supervision true`, for example `set pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end tca-supervision true`. direction accepts ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location accepts all, na, near-end or far-end (default all), so naming pm-15min/ingress/near-end scopes it exactly to the 15-minute ingress near-end counters of that one resource. The same entry also carries data-supervision (true|false). `show pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> [supported-parameters] [data-supervision] [tca-supervision]` lists the PM parameters the resource type supports for that direction and location, up to a maximum of 100 elements.

Ask the parameter object: `show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]`. type reports either counter or gauge, and units is one of na, dBm, ms, ps, ps/nm, dB, seconds, packets, events, octets, bits, blocks, times, percent, bit-ratio, C, frames, W, V, A, rpm, ps2, mA, words, cw, nm, bytes, errors or MHz. For example `show pm-parameter pm-parameter-undersized` returns units packets and type counter, and `show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds` targets a single parameter. `show pm-parameter` on its own lists all PM parameters. The same two fields come back from `show pm-catalog <catalog-name>`.

Yes, through the pm-profile object: `set pm-profile global-data-supervision auto-enabled`. global-data-supervision "provides a way to globally enable PM data-supervision without having to toggle it individually"; auto-enabled turns PM data-supervision on globally, while manual, which is the default, leaves the flag controlled via pm-profile-entry or directly per pm-control-entry. Read it back with `show pm-profile`. The pm-profile holds the information on all resources that support PM data together with their default configuration; it is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Set the per-resource-type default: `set pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-data-supervision true`. default-data-supervision means "For newly created resources of this type, whether they have PM data supervision automatically enabled or not" (true|false), and the companion default-tca-supervision does the same for threshold crossing supervision. direction takes ingress, egress, all or na (default all), location takes all, na, near-end or far-end (default all), and period is a PM period such as pm-15min or pm-24h. Read it back with `show pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> [default-data-supervision] [default-tca-supervision]`. Existing instances are still changed per resource with pm-control-entry.

Read the real-time-data-last-reset attribute of the port's pm-resource: `show pm-resource-<resource> real-time-data-last-reset`, for example `show pm-resource-trib-ptp-1-7-T9`. It is a date-and-time giving the last real-time data reset for that resource, and if the data was never reset it is the date and time of the resource's creation. The same show also returns resource-type, AID (string, 1..64 characters) and real-time-supervision (true|false, default true), and lists the pm-control-entry children such as pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end. A reset is what `clear pm real-time` performs.

Create a pm-threshold keyed to that instance: `add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/errored-seconds high-threshold <value>`, then adjust with the matching `set`, read with `show` and remove with `delete pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/errored-seconds`. direction is ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location is all, na, near-end or far-end (default all); period is a PM period such as pm-15min or pm-24h. Both low-threshold and high-threshold accept a number (uint64, int64 or decimal64), na for not applicable, or not-supported, and both default to na. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Arm the reporting with tca-supervision on the corresponding pm-control-entry.

Query the pm-threshold-profile, which holds PM configuration per parameter for a resource type: `show pm-threshold-profile-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period>/<parameter> [low-threshold] [high-threshold] [default-low-threshold] [default-high-threshold] [min-value] [max-value]`. default-low-threshold and default-high-threshold are the system defined default values for that parameter, and min-value and max-value are the minimum and maximum permitted for it; all four are show-only and take a number (uint64, int64, decimal64), na or not-supported. low-threshold and high-threshold are the configured values, settable here, for example `set pm-threshold-profile-OTUC14i/ingress/near-end/pm-24h/errored-seconds high-threshold 1200`. direction defaults to all and location defaults to all.
